user.title: Add Galaxy Fit3
user.description: Enter the watch's Bluetooth address. Unpair the watch from your phone first, wake it, and keep it near this Home Assistant host. Next, the watch shows a pairing code.

data.name: Name
data.skip_pairing: Skip pairing for now (pair on the first connection)

confirm.title: Add Galaxy Fit3
confirm.description: Do you want to set up {name}?

confirm_code.title: Confirm the pairing code
confirm_code.description:
The watch should be showing a pairing code. Home Assistant received this code:

**{code}**

Only tick the box if the code on the watch is exactly the same. If it differs, leave it unticked: the pairing will be rejected and nothing is paired.

data.matches: The code on the watch matches

abort.cannot_pair: Could not pair with the watch. Make sure it is unpaired from your phone, awake, nearby and Bluetooth is on, then try again.
abort.code_mismatch: The pairing code was not confirmed, so setup was cancelled. Nothing was paired.

progress.wait_code: Connecting to the watch and waiting for it to show a pairing code. Keep it awake and nearby.
progress.finishing: Finishing pairing and setting up the watch. This can take up to a minute; don't dismiss anything on the watch.

set_time.name: Set watch time
set_time.description: Push the current time and timezone to the watch now (also done on every connect and hourly).

is_24h.name: 24-hour format
is_24h.description: Use 24-hour clock display on the watch.

set_time_rtc.name: Set watch time (settings channel, experimental)
set_time_rtc.description: Diagnostics: send the phone's real set-time message on the settings channel (route 0b0b). Its byte layout is unconfirmed, so byte order and offset unit are selectable.

is_24h.name: 24-hour format
is_24h.description: Use 24-hour clock display on the watch.

tz_offset_seconds.name: Time zone offset (seconds)
tz_offset_seconds.description: Offset from UTC in seconds (default: Home Assistant's zone).

byte_order.name: Byte order
byte_order.description: Byte order of the multi-byte fields.

offset_unit.name: Offset unit
offset_unit.description: Whether the offset field is in seconds or minutes.

reconnect.name: Reconnect (diagnostics)
reconnect.description: Drop the link and reconnect now, optionally replaying only the first N setup frames (0 = none) to find which one resets the watch's clock.

replay_frames.name: Setup frames to replay
replay_frames.description: 0-27. Leave empty to replay all of them.

set_watch_face.name: Set watch face
set_watch_face.description: Show a watch face on the watch. A built-in face that was removed is put back.

face_id.name: Face ID
face_id.description: Face number, e.g. 79 (list_watch_faces shows the ones on the watch).

group.name: Group
group.description: Group id of the face from list_watch_faces; looked up automatically if left empty.

list_watch_faces.name: List watch faces
list_watch_faces.description: Return the faces installed on the watch (id, group, package, name).

forget_bond.name: Forget bond
forget_bond.description: Remove Home Assistant's Bluetooth bond with the watch so the next connection pairs again from scratch.

install_watch_face.name: Install watch face
install_watch_face.description: Download a watch face from the Samsung store and install it on the watch over Bluetooth Classic. Takes about a minute; the watch must be near the Home Assistant Bluetooth adapter.

face_id.name: Face ID
face_id.description: Store face number, e.g. 16 for Progress gauge 1.

style.name: Style
style.description: Style variant of the face (0 is the first).

handshake_only.name: Handshake only
handshake_only.description: Test the connection: open and close the watch's file channel without sending the face.

wait.name: Wait for the install
wait.description: Return when the face is on the watch (about a minute). Turn off to start the install and return at once; the face install sensor shows progress.

fetch_face_previews.name: Fetch face previews
fetch_face_previews.description: Save the preview pictures of store faces so the dashboard can show them. Each preview is inside the face's store package (about 4 MB), so fetching all of them downloads a few hundred MB, one package at a time in the background. Faces that already have a preview are skipped.

face_ids.name: Faces
face_ids.description: Face numbers to fetch. Leave empty for every face in the store.

data_description.is_24h: Show time in 24-hour format (off = 12-hour). Applied on the next time sync.
